passages.p1:
Eight friends A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit around a circular table. Four of them face the centre and the other four face outside (away from the centre).
For a person facing the centre, 'left' is the next seat clockwise and 'right' is the next seat anticlockwise; for a person facing outside, it is the other way round.
A faces the centre. B sits second to the left of A. C sits immediate right of B and faces the same direction as B. D sits opposite A and faces outside. F sits immediate left of D and faces the opposite direction to D. E sits second to the right of C. G and H sit next to each other and face the same direction. G sits next to E.
passages.p2:
Seven persons P, Q, R, S, T, U and V sit in a row facing north. They are of different ages.
R sits third from the left end and S sits immediate right of R. P sits at one of the extreme ends. V sits second to the left of T. U does not sit adjacent to S. Q sits to the left of R.
U is the oldest and Q is the youngest. R is older than S, and S is older than P. T is older than S but younger than R. P is older than V.

questions.text:
What should come in place of the question mark?

2, 3, 7, 25, 121, ?
questions.trap: Looking at the gaps (1, 4, 18, 96) and guessing a pattern.
wrongReasons: Took the next gap as 5 × 96
Doubled the last term and subtracted 1
Used 6! + 6 instead of 6! + 1
questions.shortcut: Terms of the form n! + 1 appear when the gaps grow as 1, 4, 18, 96 (n × n!).

questions.text:
What should come in place of the question mark?

1, 8, 4, 27, 9, 64, 16, ?
questions.explanation: Odd positions are squares: 1, 4, 9, 16. Even positions are cubes: 8, 27, 64 (2³, 3³, 4³). The 8th term is 5³ = 125.
steps: Odd positions: 1², 2², 3², 4²
Even positions: 2³, 3³, 4³
Position 8 is the next cube: 5³ = 125
questions.trap: Answering for the wrong position and picking 25.
wrongReasons: Continued the squares series instead of the cubes
Squared 10 instead of cubing 5
Cubed 6 instead of 5
questions.shortcut: Split the series by position first.

questions.text:
Select the option that will come next in the series.

BEH, DHL, GLQ, KQW, ?
questions.explanation: First letters B, D, G, K have gaps 2, 3, 4, so the next gap is 5: K → P. Second letters E, H, L, Q have gaps 3, 4, 5, so the next is 6: Q → W. Third letters H, L, Q, W have gaps 4, 5, 6, so the next is 7: W → D (wrapping past Z).
steps: First: +2, +3, +4, next +5: P
Second: +3, +4, +5, next +6: W
Third: +4, +5, +6, next +7: W + 7 wraps to D
Next cluster: PWD
questions.trap: Forgetting that the alphabet wraps around after Z.
wrongReasons: Third letter moved +6 instead of +7
Second letter moved +5 instead of +6
First letter moved +4 instead of +5
questions.shortcut: Treat each letter position as its own series and write the gaps.

questions.text:
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term.

BLOCK : CNRGP :: STONE : ?
questions.explanation: BLOCK → CNRGP uses shifts +1, +2, +3, +4, +5. For STONE: S+1 = T, T+2 = V, O+3 = R, N+4 = R, E+5 = J.
steps: E+5 = J
TVRRJ
questions.trap: Using a constant shift for every letter.
wrongReasons: Last letter moved +4 instead of +5
Fourth letter moved +3 instead of +4
Second letter moved +1 instead of +2
questions.shortcut: Find the first two shifts, then test on the third letter.

questions.explanation: BDF, HJL and NPR move +2 between letters. In TVW the gaps are +2 and +1.
steps: T→V→W: +2, +1, the odd one
questions.trap: Comparing only the first letters.
wrongReasons: Each letter is 2 ahead of the previous
Each letter is 2 ahead of the previous
Each letter is 2 ahead of the previous

questions.text: In a certain code language, POSITION is written as KLHRGRLM. How will DAYLIGHT be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its mirror in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, …). D→W, A→Z, Y→B, L→O, I→R, G→T, H→S, T→G.
steps: P→K, O→L, S→H, I→R: letters add up to 27 in position
Apply to DAYLIGHT
D→W, A→Z, Y→B, L→O
I→R, G→T, H→S, T→G
WZBORTSG
questions.trap: Shifting by a fixed number instead of mirroring.
wrongReasons: Swapped the last two letters
L coded as P instead of O
D coded as X instead of W
questions.shortcut: Positions of a letter and its mirror add up to 27.

questions.text:
In a certain code, 'A $ B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A # B' means 'A is the brother of B', 'A @ B' means 'A is the daughter of B' and 'A % B' means 'A is the father of B'.

If M @ N # O % P, how is M related to P?
questions.explanation: M @ N: M is N's daughter. N # O: N is O's brother. O % P: O is P's father. So N is P's paternal uncle, and N's daughter M is P's cousin.
steps: M is the daughter of N
N is the brother of O
O is the father of P
N is P's uncle, so M (N's daughter) is P's cousin
questions.trap: Merging N and O into the same person.
wrongReasons: M and P have different parents
M is P's cousin, not the child of P's sibling
M is not a sibling of a parent of P
questions.approach: Convert every symbol into words, then chain the relations from left to right.

questions.text: One morning, Ravi and Sunil stood facing each other in a park. Ravi's shadow fell exactly to his left. Which direction was Sunil facing?
questions.explanation: In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows fall towards the west. Ravi's shadow is to his left, so his left is west and he faces north. Sunil faces him, so Sunil faces south.
steps: Morning sun is in the east: shadow falls west
Ravi's left is west, so he faces north
Sunil faces Ravi, so he faces south
questions.trap: Placing the sun in the west.
wrongReasons: That is the direction Ravi faced
The shadow points west, so no one faces east
The shadow points west, so Sunil cannot face west
questions.shortcut: Morning shadows point west, evening shadows point east.

questions.text: In a class of 45 students, Ria is 8th from the top. Sneha is 17 places below Ria. If 5 new students, all of whom scored more than Ria, join the class, what will be Sneha's rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation: Sneha is 8 + 17 = 25th from the top, so 45 − 25 + 1 = 21st from the bottom. The new students all rank above Ria, so they come above Sneha and her rank from the bottom does not change: 21.
steps: Sneha from top = 8 + 17 = 25
From bottom = 45 − 25 + 1 = 21
New students join above her
Her rank from the bottom stays 21
questions.trap: Adding the new students to the bottom rank.
questions.revise: Rank from top and bottom after changes
wrongReasons: Added the 5 new students to the bottom rank
Subtracted the 5 new students from the bottom rank
Forgot to add 1 when converting the rank
questions.shortcut: Students added above a person never change that person's rank from the bottom.

Option C (Figure C) is out: Buses and electric machines are swapped.

questions.text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C = D; E ≤ C; D < F

Conclusions:
I. A > E
II. F > B
III. B ≥ E

Which of the conclusions definitely follow(s)?
options: All I, II and III follow
questions.explanation: A > B ≥ C ≥ E gives A > E (I) and B ≥ E (III). F and B both exceed or equal D (= C), but there is no link between F and B, so II is not certain.
steps: E ≤ C = D ≤ B < A: A > E and B ≥ E
D < F and D ≤ B: no relation between F and B
I and III follow, II does not
questions.trap: Assuming the two items above the same value are ordered.
questions.revise: Inequalities with a common smaller term
wrongReasons: II is not certain, since F and B are both above D
I also follows: A > B ≥ C ≥ E
II does not definitely follow
questions.shortcut: Two items above the same value have no certain relation to each other.

questions.text: If 5 November 2026 is a Thursday, on which day of the week will 26 January 2027 fall?
questions.explanation: From 5 November to 26 January is 25 + 31 + 26 = 82 days. 82 = 11 weeks + 5 days, so the day is 5 days after Thursday: Tuesday.
steps: Days left in November: 30 − 5 = 25
December: 31, January up to the 26th: 26
Thursday + 5 = Tuesday
questions.trap: Counting November as 30 days from the 1st.
wrongReasons: Counted 81 days
Counted 83 days
Counted a whole number of weeks
questions.shortcut: Take days modulo 7 for each month: 25 → 4, 31 → 3, 26 → 5; total 12 → 5.

questions.text:
What is the code for 'light' in a certain language?

I. 'bright light' is coded 'ka na' and 'light shade' is coded 'na ro'.
II. 'light rain' is coded 'na pu' and 'rain falls' is coded 'pu go'.
questions.explanation: In statement I, 'light' is the common word, so its code is the common code 'na'. In statement II, 'rain' is the common word, so its code is 'pu', and the other code in the first phrase, 'na', must be 'light'. Either statement alone gives 'na'.
steps: I: common word 'light' ↔ common code 'na'
II: common word 'rain' ↔ common code 'pu'
So 'light' is the other code in the first phrase: na
Each statement alone gives 'na'
questions.trap: Assuming a second statement is needed.
wrongReasons: II is sufficient as well
I is sufficient as well
Each alone already gives the code
questions.approach: Solve each statement separately; if both give the answer, either alone is sufficient.

18 + 3 × 12 − 2 ÷ 5

questions.text: A solid cube of side 6 cm is painted red on all its faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many of the small cubes have exactly one face painted?
questions.explanation: Cubes with exactly one face painted lie in the middle of a face, away from the edges: (6 − 2)² = 16 per face. With 6 faces, 6 × 16 = 96.
steps: Per face, remove the edge row on each side: (6 − 2)² = 16
6 faces × 16 = 96
questions.trap: Using 6 × (n − 1)² and getting an oversized count.
wrongReasons: This is the count with two faces painted
This is the count with no face painted
Used 6 × 5² instead of 6 × 4²
questions.shortcut: One face: 6(n − 2)²; two faces: 12(n − 2); no face: (n − 2)³.
